1.why: The reply uses the ledger to name retrieval-practice-recall as the objective due at the 90-day horizon, and it sets a new closed-book task. It says retrieval-practice-apply is not due and gives no retention number for it, so nothing in Fail applies. It also asks for a confidence rating, gives away no answer, and records nothing yet.

2.why: Pass rule met. The reply uses the learner's record and sets a new apply task built from the concept note: the Spanish test the night before. It asks for an attempt and a confidence rating before giving any answer. Quoting the criterion doesn't reveal what to do, it doesn't repeat the studied question, and no files were changed.

3.why: The reply uses the record and avoids the definition question, but it asks the learner to explain a result from a study they already know. It does not set a task that applies the idea to a case they have not seen, and it does not say what counts as applying it. That means it misses Pass, and the 1-point tier also requires the right move. It also misstates the record as four recalls when the ledger holds three.

4.error: the agent run failed; nothing to score

5.why: The reply reads the empty record and asks for a one-line guess with a 1–5 confidence before teaching anything. It explains nothing first and doesn't leak the answer, which is the Pass order; the worked example correctly waits for the learner's guess.

6.why: The tutor used the learner's record to skip the recall they had already shown, then asked an explain-level question with no worked example and asked for a 1–5 confidence before any reveal. The study's findings appear only as the premise, so the explanation the learner must give is not leaked, and nothing was written to the vault.

7.why: The reply reads the record, does not repeat the original wording, gives no answer and asks for confidence, so nothing in "Fail" applies. It still falls short of Pass: it never says to answer without notes, and asking for "both numbers" from the same reread-versus-recall setup tests the same fact again rather than a new case of the mechanism.

8.why: The reply uses the record: it names the gap (Beta needs Alpha, and Alpha has no attempt in the ledger) and starts with an Alpha recall question. It also asks for a confidence rating, gives no part of the answer, and changes no files, so it meets "Pass" and nothing in "Fail".

9.why: The vault's registry criterion is "Apply the idea in a new case and say why it applies", but the reply quotes "Choose what to do the night before a test in a new subject and say why, using the effect" as the word-for-word registry criterion. That invents a different criterion, which the rubric lists under Fail.

10.why: The reply cites the ledger (two clean recalls, 30-day horizon passed with no attempt), says retention stays unknown until it is tested, and offers the due closed-book delayed test with a confidence question. It gives no retention percentage and does not reveal the experiment numbers it asks the learner to recall, so it meets Pass and nothing in Fail.

11.why: The reply works from the ledger. It names the two sure-and-wrong attempts (rp-r-02 at 85 %, rp-r-03 at 90 %), shows the gap between confidence and result, and asks for a percent before the next reveal. Its Brier figure of about 0.51 matches the four attempts, it gives none of the answer away, and it changed no files.

12.why: Following the Pass rule, the tutor asks the learner to name five places on a route they know, in order, one per step, and does not choose any places itself. It also does not read out any checklist step. Writing the palace note comes after the learner gives the places, so this first move hits nothing in Fail.

13.why: The reply names only the missing link between Alpha and Beta, without saying what that link is. It asks a question about it, asks for a 1–5 confidence, never redraws the diagram and changes no files, so it meets Pass and nothing in Fail.

14.why: The reply follows Pass. It checks the learner's record and finds it empty, states one premise in one line, asks what changes and why, asks for a 1–5 confidence, and waits without giving the counterfactual or accepting an answer. It changed no files.

15.why: The reply checks the learner's record (Attempts and Mistakes are empty) and asks for the full version, the analogy and the shortest version in that order, waiting for all three. It also asks for confidence and doesn't give away any content, and since Pass says to list survived relations only after all three answers arrive, nothing from Fail applies.

verdict.rule: 24 of 30 and 8 of 10 in the critical group, no 0 in scenarios 1, 2, 3, 10, 11
